RAFAEL MORETTI-KLEIN
Backend Engineer (Python) | Principal Software Engineer
Munich, Germany | rafael.morettiklein@example.com | +49 555 0505 505 | linkedin.com/in/rmk-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building production systems in Python, Go and C++. Experienced in backend services, API platforms, distributed systems and relational databases, including PostgreSQL. Led development of high-throughput services and platform migrations, improving playback API availability to 99.95%. Fluent in English, with a track record of documenting architecture decisions and communicating technical trade-offs.

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE

Director of Engineering, Platform | Streamhaus GmbH (video streaming), Munich
2019 – Aug 2026
- Led the platform organisation of 5 teams, 45 engineers and 5 engineering managers, responsible for identity, playback API, billing integration and developer platform.
- Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services on GKE; improved playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.
- Reduced cloud spend by 31% (€4.2M per year) through rightsizing, committed use discounts and an internal cost dashboard.
- Introduced an RFC process, architecture review board and on-call guidelines adopted company-wide.
- Grew the organisation from 18 to 45 engineers and conducted more than 200 interviews.

Principal Engineer | Streamhaus GmbH
2015 – 2019
- Served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, an internal framework similar to FastAPI, Cassandra and Redis.
- Designed an entitlement service handling 120,000 requests per second at peak, using Go and Cassandra.
- Co-authored the company’s service template and Python style guide.

Senior Software Engineer | Nordfels Telematik AG, Stuttgart
2010 – 2015
- Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS and RabbitMQ.
- Led a team of 6 developers on the route-history product.

Software Engineer | Dataquelle Systems GmbH, Karlsruhe
2005 – 2010
- Developed C++ and Python software for industrial data acquisition on Linux and embedded x86.
- Built a Python test harness used by QA for 8 years.

EDUCATION
Dipl.-Inf. (equivalent MSc), Computer Science | Rhine Valley University, 2005

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming: Python (Django, Flask, FastAPI, Tornado, asyncio), Go, C++ (older)
Databases and messaging: PostgreSQL/PostGIS, Cassandra, Redis, Kafka, RabbitMQ
Cloud and infrastructure: GCP (GKE, Pub/Sub, BigQuery), AWS (EC2, S3), Kubernetes, Terraform
APIs and observability: gRPC, Protobuf, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry
Other: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management

LANGUAGES
German (native), Italian (native), English (fluent)

PUBLICATIONS & TALKS
- “Running Python at 100k rps” – EuroPython-style conference talk, 2018
- “Cost is a feature” – internal platform engineering summit keynote, 2023

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and achievement-oriented. It presents substantial backend, Python, distributed-systems, cloud, reliability, and engineering-leadership experience with strong metrics such as 99.95% availability, 120,000 requests per second, 300,000 vehicles, and €4.2M annual savings. The chronology is clear and the content is easy to scan. Its main content weakness is that it is positioned partly as a principal/director-level profile while the target role is an individual-contributor backend engineering position; the document should make recent hands-on backend relevance clearer without overstating current coding activity.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, simple text formatting, reverse chronology, and searchable technology keywords, so it should parse reliably in most ATS systems. Relevant terms include Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, AWS, and automated testing-related experience through the Python test harness. AI screening probability is high for Python, backend services, cloud deployment, PostgreSQL, event streaming, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code, observability, and seniority. Screening may be weaker for Docker, REST APIs, schema migrations, query tuning, CI/CD, and GitHub Actions because these are not supported by the candidate information and therefore should not be added. The phrase “internal framework similar to FastAPI” is less ATS-friendly than the supported FastAPI keyword already present in the Skills section.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for Python backend engineering, high-throughput services, API platforms, cloud deployment, distributed systems, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, technical documentation processes, and production reliability. The candidate clearly exceeds the experience requirement and demonstrates relevant transport-domain adjacency through fleet telematics, GPS ingestion, and a route-history product. English fluency is shown. The CV does not establish Docker, REST API design/consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD, or GitHub Actions. It also does not show logistics freight-forwarding, shipment tracking, EDI, Dutch, or French experience. These are candidate-background gaps or unsupported requirements rather than defects that can be repaired by rewriting. The leadership-heavy profile may also appear overqualified for a seven-engineer team, although the strong hands-on backend history remains relevant.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the Professional Summary, remove the unsupported claims “track record of documenting architecture decisions” and “communicating technical trade-offs.” The Original Candidate Information supports RFCs, architecture reviews, a Python style guide, and an English-fluent language profile, but it does not explicitly support those broader claims. Replace the final sentence with a truthful version such as: “Fluent in English, with experience introducing RFCs, architecture reviews, and company-wide on-call guidelines.”

MINOR — In the Principal Engineer experience entry, change “using Python, Tornado, an internal framework similar to FastAPI” to “using Python, Tornado, and an internal web framework; FastAPI is also listed in the technical skills.” Do not imply that the internal framework was FastAPI. This preserves the supported FastAPI keyword while avoiding a potentially misleading equivalence.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary, make the target role’s hands-on backend relevance more prominent by changing the opening to: “Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building production systems in Python, Go, and C++.” Retain the existing backend services, API platforms, distributed systems, PostgreSQL, and availability achievements after that sentence. This better matches the advertised Backend Engineer position without removing seniority or inventing current coding responsibilities.

MINOR — In the Senior Software Engineer entry under Nordfels Telematik AG, retain the existing fleet-telematics and GPS-ingestion bullet but use the job-relevant wording “transport” and “route history” only as supported by the source: “Built backend systems for fleet telematics, ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, and RabbitMQ; led the route-history product team of 6 developers.” This makes the strongest logistics-adjacent experience easier for recruiters and ATS systems to identify without claiming freight-forwarding or shipment-tracking experience.
critique.critical_issues:
Potential hallucination: The Professional Summary claims a “track record of documenting architecture decisions and communicating technical trade-offs,” but the Original Candidate Information does not explicitly substantiate either claim. Remove or replace these phrases as specified in the improvement instructions. No other material hallucinations were identified.
Claims the sources (the candidate's own material; for the employer, the job ad and company research) do not support:
- "communicating technical trade-offs"

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, concise, professional, and achievement-focused. It presents substantial backend, platform, reliability, cloud, and engineering leadership experience with strong measurable results, including 99.95% API availability, 120,000 requests per second, 31% cloud-cost reduction, and services processing data from 300,000 vehicles. The main content weakness is that several bullets emphasize leadership and architecture rather than the hands-on backend responsibilities of this role. One bullet also contains awkward explanatory wording: “FastAPI is also listed in the technical skills,” which reads like a drafting note rather than CV content. The document does not clearly establish several core requirements, particularly REST API design and consumption, PostgreSQL query tuning and schema migrations, Docker, automated testing, and CI/CD.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly conventional headings, reverse-chronological experience, plain text, and relevant keywords such as Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, AWS, and GCP. The categorized skills section is easy to parse. ATS matching would improve if supported terms from the advertisement were used more explicitly, especially REST APIs, automated testing, CI/CD, Docker, schema migrations, query tuning, cloud deployment, and event ingestion. Do not add unsupported tools or practices. The phrase “FastAPI is also listed in the technical skills” should be removed because it is not a professional accomplishment and may reduce screening quality. The document has a strong technical keyword profile, but AI screening may classify the candidate as primarily an engineering director or principal-level leader rather than as a hands-on backend engineer unless the experience section foregrounds direct implementation and service ownership.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV is a strong match for Python backend engineering, high-throughput APIs, distributed systems, PostgreSQL, cloud platforms, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, architecture discussions, on-call practices, and clear technical documentation. The fleet-telematics work provides relevant transport-domain experience, including GPS ingestion from 300,000 vehicles and a route-history product. English fluency and communication of technical trade-offs are supported by the RFC process, architecture review board, Python style guide, and conference presentations. The candidate exceeds the experience requirement and aligns well with the company's reliability, ownership, documentation, and continuous-improvement culture. However, the candidate material does not establish Docker, PostgreSQL query tuning, safe schema migrations, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, or explicit REST API design and consumption. It also does not provide evidence of EDI formats, Dutch, or French. These are candidate-evidence gaps rather than writing defects and should not be represented as capabilities without supporting information.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH PRIORITY
1. In the Principal Engineer experience entry, remove the wording “FastAPI is also listed in the technical skills.” Replace the full bullet with a professional, factual version such as: “Served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, an internal web framework, Cassandra, and Redis.” This avoids meta-commentary and does not overstate the internal framework as FastAPI.

2. In the Professional Summary, revise the emphasis so the first sentence foregrounds hands-on backend engineering rather than leadership. For example: “Backend engineer and engineering leader with 21 years of experience building production services and APIs in Python, Go, and C++.” Retain the leadership experience afterward.

3. In the Director of Engineering experience entry, revise the migration bullet to make cloud deployment and service ownership more explicit without adding unsupported Docker claims. For example: “Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services deployed on GKE, improving playback API availability from 99.5% to 99.95%.”

4. In the Senior Software Engineer entry, make the transport-domain relevance more visible by changing the first bullet to: “Built backend fleet-telematics systems ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, and RabbitMQ.” This directly matches the role’s event-ingestion and transport-platform context.

5. In the Technical Skills section, retain the current supported technologies but do not list Docker, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, REST, schema migrations, or query tuning as skills unless they are confirmed by the candidate. The current CV should not imply these requirements are met when the original candidate information does not support them.

MINOR / TARGETED ENHANCEMENTS
6. In the Technical Skills section, change “APIs and observability” to “APIs, messaging, and observability” only if the formatting allows it, and retain the supported terms “gRPC,” “Protobuf,” “Prometheus,” “Grafana,” and “OpenTelemetry.” This better reflects the existing technical evidence without inventing REST experience.

7. In the Professional Summary, change “Fluent in English” to “English (fluent)” or leave the language proficiency solely in the Languages section. Avoid duplicating the same information unless the summary needs the explicit job keyword.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, professional CV with clear chronological structure, substantial quantified achievements, and credible senior backend engineering experience. The strongest evidence includes the migration to approximately 60 Python/Go services, 99.95% API availability, 120,000 requests per second, 300,000 vehicles, cloud-cost reduction, and company-wide engineering practices. The document is concise and readable. Its main content limitation is that some relevant capabilities are listed only in the Skills section rather than demonstrated in the experience bullets, particularly testing, Kafka, observability, Terraform, and AWS. The profile also presents a very senior Director/Principal background for a Backend Engineer role, so it would benefit from foregrounding hands-on backend/API contribution more explicitly without overstating current coding activity.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: standard section headings, simple text structure, conventional dates, recognizable technology names, and no problematic graphics, tables, headers, or footers. It contains strong matches such as Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, Prometheus, Grafana, OpenTelemetry, GCP, AWS, APIs, distributed systems, and automated testing-related experience. AI screening probability is high for the Python backend, cloud, platform reliability, database, event-streaming, Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, and observability aspects of the role. It is weaker for exact-match screening because Docker, REST APIs, query tuning, schema migrations, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, EKS, EDI, and logistics terminology are not supported by the candidate information. These should not be added without evidence. The current use of "APIs" and "playback API" is truthful, but does not establish REST specifically.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a strong overall match for Python backend engineering, cloud deployment, high-throughput services, API reliability, event/data ingestion, PostgreSQL, Kafka, Kubernetes, Terraform, observability, technical communication, architecture discussions, and on-call practices. The fleet-telematics work involving GPS data from 300,000 vehicles provides relevant transport-domain context, although it does not establish freight forwarding, shipment tracking, or EDI experience. The candidate's seniority is substantially above the role's stated few-years backend profile, which may prompt questions about fit for a seven-engineer team, but the CV already presents both leadership and technical experience. The material does not establish Docker, PostgreSQL query tuning, schema migrations, REST API design/consumption, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, EDI formats, or Dutch/French language skills. These are candidate-background gaps rather than document defects.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE IMPROVEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Summary, make the hands-on backend/API relevance more prominent by replacing the second sentence with a more evidence-led version such as: "Built and led large-scale backend services and APIs in Python, Go, and C++, including a migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 services on GKE and a playback API improved to 99.95% availability." This uses evidence already present in the CV and reduces the impression that the profile is exclusively managerial.
2. In the Principal Engineer experience section, change "Served as technical lead for the playback API, using Python, Tornado, an internal web framework, Cassandra, and Redis" to "Served as technical lead for the playback API, designing and operating backend API services with Python, Tornado, an internal web framework, Cassandra, and Redis." This makes the existing API-design relevance more explicit without claiming REST.
3. In the Senior Software Engineer section, change "Built backend fleet-telematics systems ingesting GPS data from 300,000 vehicles" to "Built backend fleet-telematics systems that ingested GPS data from 300,000 vehicles using C++, Python, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, and RabbitMQ." This improves alignment with the role's event-ingestion and transport-domain language while remaining fully supported.
4. In Technical Skills, replace the broad "Other" category with more searchable, evidence-based categories: "Testing: Python test harnesses" and "Engineering practices: Distributed systems design, architecture reviews, technical hiring, people management." Do not add CI/CD or Docker, which are not supported by the source material.
5. In the Streamhaus Director experience section, change "Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go services deployed on GKE" to "Drove migration from a Python 2 monolith to approximately 60 Python and Go backend services deployed on GKE." This adds the target role's backend terminology while preserving the original claim.
6. Keep the current section headings and plain-text formatting. Do not add unsupported keywords such as Docker, REST, schema migrations, query tuning, CI/CD, GitHub Actions, EDI, EDIFACT, or X12 merely to improve ATS matching.
